Not a git repo (as noted in the environment info), so no commit is needed. The implementation is complete.

## Summary

Implemented ticket 2 (happy path for `PUT`/`GET` blob) in `server/src/main/scala/syncbox/server/Server.scala`:

- Registered a `/blobs/` context alongside the existing `/healthz` one.
- **`PUT /blobs/{key}`** — creates parent directories via `Files.createDirectories`, streams the request body straight to disk through a `DigestOutputStream` (SHA-256) using `InputStream.transferTo` to get size and hash in one pass, then returns `201` with hand-built JSON `{"key","sha256","size"}` (key is escaped for JSON safety).
- **`GET /blobs/{key}`** — streams the file back with `application/octet-stream` and `200`, or `404` if it doesn't exist.
- Other methods on `/blobs/{key}` get `405` with an `Allow` header; unexpected exceptions are caught and turned into `500` rather than crashing the exchange — kept minimal, no traversal validation, no atomic rename, no listing/delete (all explicitly out of scope per the ticket).
- Key is taken from `exchange.getRequestURI.getPath` (already percent-decoded), stripped of the `/blobs/` prefix, so nested keys like `docs/readme.txt` resolve naturally via `Path.resolve`.

Added `server/src/test/scala/syncbox/server/BlobsSpec.scala` covering round-trip byte fidelity, JSON field correctness (key/sha256/size), nested-directory creation, 404 on missing key, overwrite behavior, and empty-body blobs.

Verified via `docker compose build` (all 20 tests pass, including the 6 new ones) and an end-to-end smoke test through `run-server` + real HTTP calls (PUT/GET for top-level and nested keys, 404 for missing keys, on-disk contents and sha256 confirmed byte-for-byte). No changes needed to Dockerfile/docker-compose.yml/run-server — they already covered this.
